## Staggered adoption

- In chapter 4, the treatment starts at **one date** for all treated units.
- Most policies **roll out**: units adopt at different dates, and some never adopt.
- Running example: **unilateral divorce** in the US. From 1970, states let one spouse end
  the marriage without the other's consent. Most states adopt in the 1970s, some never do.
- Stevenson and Wolfers (2006) estimate its effect on **women's suicide**.

\begin{center}
\includegraphics[height=0.3\textheight]{fig/cartoon.jpg}
\end{center}

\vfill
\footnotesize\emph{Reference for the whole chapter: Baker, Callaway, Cunningham,
Goodman-Bacon \& Sant'Anna (2026), ``Difference-in-Differences Designs: A Practitioner's
Guide''.}

## Roadmap

1. **Setting**: cohorts and comparison groups.
2. **The problem**: what TWFE computes when adoption is staggered.
3. **The solution**: one $2\times2$ per cohort and date, three comparison groups, three
   estimators.
4. **Aggregation** and conclusion.

# Setting

## Cohorts and comparison groups

- **Cohort** $g_i$: the date at which unit $i$ is first treated ($g_i=\infty$ if never
  treated).
- **Event time** $k=t-g_i$: the number of periods since adoption.
- At date $t$, a unit is **treated**, **not yet treated** or **never treated**. In 1976:

\begin{center}
\begin{tikzpicture}[x=0.8cm,y=0.75cm,font=\footnotesize]
  % lanes: grey = untreated, accent = treated
  \foreach \y/\g/\lab in {3/3/{Adopts in 1973}, 2/7/{Adopts in 1977}, 1/11/{Never adopts}} {
    \node[anchor=east] at (-0.3,\y) {\lab};
    \draw[gray!60, line width=1.2pt] (0,\y) -- (10,\y);
    \ifnum\g<11 \draw[accent, line width=3pt] (\g,\y) -- (10,\y); \fi
  }
  % 1976
  \draw[dashed, gray] (6,0.35) -- (6,3.45);
  \foreach \y in {1,2,3} \fill[black] (6,\y) circle (2.2pt);
  \node[above=2pt, fill=white, inner sep=1.5pt, text=accent, font=\scriptsize\bfseries] at (6,3) {treated ($k=3$)};
  \node[above=2pt, fill=white, inner sep=1.5pt, font=\scriptsize\bfseries] at (6,2) {not yet treated};
  \node[above=2pt, fill=white, inner sep=1.5pt, font=\scriptsize\bfseries] at (6,1) {never treated};
  % time axis
  \draw[->] (0,0.3) -- (10.4,0.3);
  \foreach \x in {0,...,10} {
    \draw (\x,0.38) -- (\x,0.22);
    \pgfmathtruncatemacro{\yr}{1970+\x}
    \ifnum\x=6 \node[below, font=\scriptsize\bfseries] at (\x,0.22) {\yr};
    \else \node[below, font=\scriptsize] at (\x,0.22) {\yr}; \fi
  }
\end{tikzpicture}
\end{center}

- Not-yet-treated and never-treated units are the two possible **comparison groups**.

# TWFE

## The static TWFE under staggered adoption

$$ y_{it}=f_i+f_t+\beta\,d_{it}+u_{it},\qquad d_{it}=\mathbf{1}\{t\ge g_i\} $$

- $\hat\beta$ is a weighted average of **all** the $2\times2$ DiDs in the data
  (Goodman-Bacon 2021).
- With an early cohort, a late cohort and never-treated units, there are four $2\times2$s:
  - early cohort against never-treated units;
  - late cohort against never-treated units;
  - early cohort against the late cohort, **before** the late cohort is treated;
  - late cohort against the early cohort, **already treated**: a **forbidden comparison**.
- The weights depend on group sizes and on the timing, not on the question asked.

## The forbidden comparison

\begin{center}
\begin{tikzpicture}[x=0.8cm,y=0.6cm,font=\footnotesize]
  % comparison windows (drawn first, behind the lanes)
  \fill[gray!15] (3,1.6) rectangle (7,3.4);
  \fill[accent!15] (7,1.6) rectangle (10,3.4);
  \draw[accent, thick] (7,1.6) rectangle (10,3.4);
  \node[align=center, font=\scriptsize] at (5,3.95) {clean: early vs late,\\ late not yet treated};
  \node[align=center, font=\scriptsize\bfseries, text=accent] at (8.5,3.95) {forbidden: late vs early,\\ early already treated};
  % lanes: grey = untreated, accent = treated
  \foreach \y/\g/\lab in {3/3/{Early (1973)}, 2/7/{Late (1977)}, 1/11/{Never}} {
    \node[anchor=east] at (-0.3,\y) {\lab};
    \draw[gray!60, line width=1.2pt] (0,\y) -- (10,\y);
    \ifnum\g<11 \draw[accent, line width=3pt] (\g,\y) -- (10,\y); \fi
  }
  % time axis
  \draw[->] (0,0.3) -- (10.4,0.3);
  \foreach \x in {0,...,10} {
    \draw (\x,0.38) -- (\x,0.22);
    \pgfmathtruncatemacro{\yr}{1970+\x}
    \node[below, font=\scriptsize] at (\x,0.22) {\yr};
  }
\end{tikzpicture}
\end{center}

\small

- From 1977, TWFE compares the late cohort with the early cohort, **already treated**.
- The early cohort's outcome still moves because of its own treatment: its change is not
  a counterfactual.
- TWFE subtracts this change. The early cohort's effect receives a **negative weight**
  (de Chaisemartin and D'Haultfœuille 2020), and $\hat\beta$ can shrink or even change
  sign.
- Divorce: TWFE gives $-3.1$ suicides per million women, $-5.4$ without the forbidden
  comparisons (Goodman-Bacon 2021).

## The dynamic TWFE

$$ y_{it}=f_i+f_t+\sum_{k\neq-1}\beta_k\,\mathbf{1}\{t-g_i=k\}+u_{it} $$

- The event-study regression has the same problem (Sun and Abraham 2021).
- Each $\hat\beta_k$ mixes the effect $k$ periods after adoption with the effects of
  **other cohorts at other dates**.
- The early cohorts' effects can appear in the **pre-period** coefficients, as if parallel
  trends failed.
- The problem disappears only if all cohorts have the same effect.

# Solution

## The solution: choose the comparison group

- TWFE mixes **all** the $2\times2$s, forbidden ones included.
- Instead, estimate $\text{ATT}(g,t)$, the effect at date $t$ for the units first treated
  at $g$, against a comparison group **chosen** by the researcher.
- Choosing the comparison group is choosing a parallel-trends assumption.
- The $\text{ATT}(g,t)$ are then averaged.

## Example: the comparison group for $\text{ATT}(1973,t)$

\begin{center}
\begin{tikzpicture}[x=0.8cm,y=0.65cm,font=\footnotesize]
  % lanes: grey = untreated, accent = treated
  \foreach \y/\g/\lab in {3/3/{Adopts in 1973}, 2/7/{Adopts in 1977}, 1/11/{Never adopts}} {
    \node[anchor=east] at (-0.3,\y) {\lab};
    \draw[gray!60, line width=1.2pt] (0,\y) -- (10,\y);
    \ifnum\g<11 \draw[accent, line width=3pt] (\g,\y) -- (10,\y); \fi
  }
  % base period g-1 = 1972 and date t = 1976
  \draw[dashed, gray] (2,0.35) -- (2,3.55);
  \draw[dashed, gray] (6,0.35) -- (6,3.55);
  \draw[dashed, gray] (9,0.35) -- (9,3.55);
  \node[above, font=\scriptsize\bfseries] at (2,3.55) {base: $g-1=1972$};
  \node[above, font=\scriptsize\bfseries] at (6,3.55) {$t=1976$};
  \node[above, font=\scriptsize\bfseries] at (9,3.55) {$t=1979$};
  \foreach \y in {1,2,3} { \fill[black] (2,\y) circle (2pt); \fill[black] (6,\y) circle (2pt); }
  \foreach \y in {1,3} \fill[black] (9,\y) circle (2pt);
  % 1977 adopters are already treated in 1979: excluded from the comparison group
  \draw[white, line width=4.5pt] (8.75,1.72) -- (9.25,2.28) (8.75,2.28) -- (9.25,1.72);
  \draw[red, line width=2.5pt] (8.75,1.72) -- (9.25,2.28) (8.75,2.28) -- (9.25,1.72);
  % time axis
  \draw[->] (0,0.3) -- (10.4,0.3);
  \foreach \x in {0,...,10} {
    \draw (\x,0.38) -- (\x,0.22);
    \pgfmathtruncatemacro{\yr}{1970+\x}
    \node[below, font=\scriptsize] at (\x,0.22) {\yr};
  }
\end{tikzpicture}
\end{center}

- The effect in 1976 for the states that adopted in 1973: their change from 1972 to 1976,
  minus the change of the comparison group over the same years.
- Comparison group = **never-treated**: the states that never adopt.
- Comparison group = **not-yet-treated**: the states that never adopt **and** the states
  that adopt in 1977, still untreated in 1976.
- For a later date, say 1979, the states that adopt in 1977 are already treated and leave
  the not-yet-treated group: its composition changes with $t$.

## Three parallel-trends assumptions

\begin{center}
\small
\begin{tabular}{@{}lll@{}}
\toprule
Assumption & Comparison group & Base period\\
\midrule
\textbf{PT-never} & never-treated units & $g-1$\\[3pt]
\textbf{PT-not-yet} & units not yet treated at $t$, never-treated included & $g-1$\\[3pt]
\textbf{PT-all} & not-yet-treated units & all pre-periods\\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{center}

\vspace{6pt}

- PT-never and PT-not-yet assume parallel trends only **after** $g-1$.
- PT-all also assumes them **before**, so the pre-trends become a test of the assumption.

## Three estimators

\begin{center}
\small
\begin{tabular}{@{}>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{3.3cm} >{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{2.1cm} >{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{5.3cm}@{}}
\toprule
Estimator & Assumption & How it works\\
\midrule
Callaway and Sant'Anna (2021) & PT-never or PT-not-yet & computes each $\text{ATT}(g,t)$ as a $2\times2$, then averages them\\[4pt]
Sun and Abraham (2021) & PT-never & the same effects, from a regression with one dummy per cohort and event time\\[4pt]
Imputation (Borusyak et al. 2024; Gardner 2022) & PT-all & estimates the fixed effects on untreated observations, then predicts the untreated outcome of treated ones\\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{center}

\vfill
\footnotesize\emph{Other estimators: stacked regressions (Cengiz et al. 2019); de Chaisemartin
and D'Haultfœuille (2020), which also handle treatments that switch off (chapter 6).}

## Choosing an assumption

- **PT-all** (imputation): the most **precise**, but biased if the pre-trends are not
  parallel.
- **PT-never**: a comparison group of **fixed composition**, but never-treated units may be
  **too few** or **too different**.
- **PT-not-yet**: more comparison units than PT-never, but their composition **changes**
  with $t$.

\begin{alertblock}{Not a robustness check}
The estimators rest on different assumptions, so their estimates differ. Report the
estimator of the assumption you can defend; a gap with the others shows which assumption
the result depends on.
\end{alertblock}

# Aggregation

## Aggregation

- Each $\text{ATT}(g,t)$ compares a **treated cohort**, the units first treated at $g$,
  with a **comparison group**, never-treated or not-yet-treated units.
- Forbidden comparisons concern the comparison group. **Aggregation concerns the treated
  cohorts.**
- The event study averages, for each $k$, the effects **of the treated cohorts** observed
  $k$ years after adoption.
- The late cohorts are observed **for fewer years** after adoption, so the cohorts in the
  average **change with $k$**.

## Example: unequal windows

\begin{center}
\begin{tikzpicture}[x=0.8cm,y=0.55cm,font=\footnotesize]
  % lanes: grey = untreated, accent = treated, with event time k above the treated years
  \foreach \y/\g/\lab in {4.0/3/{Adopts in 1973}, 1.6/7/{Adopts in 1977}} {
    \node[anchor=east] at (-0.3,\y) {\lab};
    \draw[gray!60, line width=1.2pt] (0,\y) -- (10,\y);
    \draw[accent, line width=3pt] (\g,\y) -- (10,\y);
    \foreach \x in {\g,...,10} {
      \pgfmathtruncatemacro{\k}{\x-\g}
      \node[above, font=\scriptsize, text=accent] at (\x,\y) {\k};
    }
  }
  % braces over the observed post-adoption windows
  \draw[decorate, decoration={brace, amplitude=5pt}, thick]
    (3,4.65) -- (10,4.65) node[midway, above=5pt] {observed up to $k=7$};
  \draw[decorate, decoration={brace, amplitude=5pt}, thick]
    (7,2.25) -- (10,2.25) node[midway, above=5pt] {observed up to $k=3$};
  % time axis
  \draw[->] (0,0.6) -- (10.4,0.6);
  \foreach \x in {0,...,10} {
    \draw (\x,0.68) -- (\x,0.52);
    \pgfmathtruncatemacro{\yr}{1970+\x}
    \node[below, font=\scriptsize] at (\x,0.52) {\yr};
  }
\end{tikzpicture}
\end{center}

- Data stop in 1980: the 1973 states are observed up to $k=7$, the 1977 states only up to
  $k=3$.
- From $k=0$ to $k=3$, the event study averages the two cohorts. **From $k=4$ on, it
  covers only the 1973 states.**
- A jump between $k=3$ and $k=4$ can therefore come from the 1977 states leaving the
  average, with no change in the effect.
- Either keep a window common to all cohorts ($k\le3$ here), or say it.

## Conclusion

1. **Define the target**: which effects, which average.
2. **Choose the comparison group**, that is the parallel-trends assumption, and defend it.
3. **Estimate** with the corresponding estimator.
4. **Check** the pre-trends and compare with the neighbouring assumption.

\begin{block}{On TWFE}
``It has well-understood, potentially serious, and easily remedied problems, and we do not
recommend using it.'' --- Baker et al. (2026)
\end{block}

# In R

## What you must build in the data

These estimators need the **timing** structure explicitly:

- the **cohort** $g_i$ — each unit's first treatment period, on *all* of its rows;
- **event time** $k=t-g_i$;
- a **never-treated** indicator (or the last-treated cohort as never-treated, dropping the
  periods where everyone is treated);
- units treated in the **first** period have no pre-period: drop them.

Software builds the $2\times2$s and the aggregation for you — you supply $g_i$ and the
**assumption**.

## In R: the timing variables (data.table)

Six lines build the variables the authors' R packages need, with `data.table`.

```r
library(data.table); library(fixest); library(did)
library(did2s); library(HonestDiD)
d <- fread("rica_bio_td5.csv")                                 # 1
d[, e := fifelse(cohorte > 0, annee - cohorte, NA_integer_)]   # 2
d[, traite := as.integer(cohorte > 0 & annee >= cohorte)]      # 3
d[, ee := e]; d[ee < -4 | ee > 5 | is.na(ee), ee := -1000L]    # 4
d[, g_sa := fifelse(cohorte == 0, 10000L, cohorte)]            # 5
d[, reg_an := paste(region, annee)]                            # 6
```

\small

- **1** — one row per farm `id` and year `annee`; `cohorte` is $g_i$, the conversion
  year, 0 if never converted; `y` on the next slides stands for the outcome column.
- **2** — event time $k = t - g_i$, missing if never converted (`d[, x := ...]` adds a
  column; `fifelse` is a vectorised if).
- **3** — $d_{it} = \mathbf{1}\{t \ge g_i\}$, the treatment indicator of TWFE.
- **4** — event time **binned**: outside $[-4, 5]$ and never converted get a reference code.
- **5** — the cohort as `sunab` wants it: never converted coded as a far-future cohort.
- **6** — the region $\times$ year label of the fixed effect.

## In R: TWFE and Sun–Abraham (fixest)

Four lines estimate the regression to avoid and its saturated correction.

```r
tw <- feols(y ~ traite | id + reg_an, d, cluster = ~id)        # 1
sa <- feols(y ~ sunab(g_sa, annee, ref.p = -1) | id + reg_an,
            d, cluster = ~id)                                  # 2
summary(sa, agg = "ATT")                                       # 3
coeftable(sa)                                                  # 4
```

\small

- **1** — TWFE: the outcome on $d_{it}$ with farm and region $\times$ year effects,
  standard errors clustered by farm. Its coefficient is the weighted average of
  $2\times2$s of the chapter, forbidden comparisons included.
- **2** — Sun–Abraham: `sunab(cohort, period)` builds every cohort $\times$ event-time
  dummy, with $k = -1$ as reference; the never converted are the only control.
- **3** — aggregates the cohort $\times$ time coefficients into one ATT with the
  cohort shares as weights.
- **4** — the event-study coefficients, one per $k$, with their standard errors.

## In R: imputation (did2s)

Two lines estimate the PT-all analogue and test its pre-trends.

```r
imp <- did2s(d, yname = "y", first_stage = ~ 0 | id + reg_an,
             second_stage = ~ i(ee, ref = c(-1, -1000)),
             treatment = "traite", cluster_var = "id")         # 1
wald(imp, keep = "ee::-[2-4]$")                                # 2
```

\small

- **1** — imputation in two stages. `first_stage`: the fixed effects are estimated on
  the **untreated cells only**, those where `traite` is 0. `second_stage`: the outcome
  net of those effects is regressed on the event-time dummies, `i(ee, ...)`, with
  $k = -1$ and the binned code as references. Standard errors clustered by farm.
- **2** — the joint test that the coefficients of $k = -4, -3, -2$ are zero. fixest names
  the dummies `ee::-4`, `ee::-3`, \dots; `keep` selects them by a pattern on the name.
  This is the pre-trend check of PT-all.

## In R: Callaway–Sant'Anna (did)

Two lines estimate every $\text{ATT}(g,t)$ and aggregate them by event time.

```r
a <- att_gt(yname = "y", tname = "annee", idname = "id",
            gname = "cohorte", data = d,
            control_group = "notyettreated",
            base_period = "universal",
            allow_unbalanced_panel = TRUE)                     # 1
aggte(a, type = "dynamic", min_e = -4, max_e = 5)             # 2
```

\small

- **1** — one $\text{ATT}(g,t)$ per cohort and year, each a $2\times2$ against the
  **not-yet-treated**; `"nevertreated"` gives the other assumption. `"universal"` takes
  $g-1$ as the base period for the pre-periods too (the default compares each pre-period
  with the previous one). On a rotating panel, `allow_unbalanced_panel` makes the package
  treat the data as repeated cross-sections.
- **2** — aggregates the $\text{ATT}(g,t)$ by event time, from $-4$ to $5$;
  `type = "simple"` returns a single ATT instead.

## In R: how much violation survives (HonestDiD)

Three lines bound the effect at one event time under a limited violation of parallel
trends.

```r
beta <- coef(imp); V <- vcov(imp)                              # 1
hd <- createSensitivityResults_relativeMagnitudes(
        betahat = beta, sigma = V, numPrePeriods = 3,
        numPostPeriods = 6, Mbarvec = c(0.5, 1, 1.5, 2),
        l_vec = basisVector(4, 6))                             # 2
hd[, c("Mbar", "lb", "ub")]                                    # 3
```

\small

- **1** — the event-study coefficients of the imputation and their covariance, ordered
  from $k = -4$ to $k = 5$: three pre-periods ($-4,-3,-2$) and six post ($0,\dots,5$);
  check the order with `names(beta)`.
- **2** — Rambachan–Roth: for each $\bar M$, the interval that stays valid if the
  post-treatment deviation from parallel trends is at most $\bar M$ times the largest
  pre-treatment one; `l_vec` selects the fourth post period, $k = 3$.
- **3** — one row per $\bar M$ with the bounds. The first $\bar M$ whose interval
  contains zero measures how thin the margin is.
